question.text: In Bollinger Band analysis, a stock is considered 'overbought' when its price goes:

answer.text: Two standard deviations below the moving average
Two standard deviations above the moving average
Exactly at the moving average level
One standard deviation above the moving average

explanation.text: The Logic: Bollinger Bands use normal distribution — when the price moves two standard deviations above the moving average, the stock is considered overbought (potential sell signal). Conversely, two standard deviations below indicates oversold (potential buy signal). The Trap: Two standard deviations below is oversold, not overbought — the directions are opposite. Cross-Exam Context: Technical indicators like Bollinger Bands are tested in X-A and VIII.
